versions.summary: Each turn it simulates ownership and small enclosures along legal routes, then follows the best positive discounted income gain. It detours for qualifying non-Purge pickups when their value beats the route score threshold, and avoids Purge pickups throughout.
versions.tagline: Replans six moves ahead, choosing routes by simulated territory income and worthwhile power-ups.

versions.summary: It keeps growing connected territory, targets the less-contested nearby hotspot, and pursues valuable pickups while avoiding the rivals’ immediate area. Purge Cache is eligible only when its pickup would wipe strictly more enemy cells than your own; otherwise the bot avoids it.
versions.tagline: Build safely, take valuable hotspots, and collect only power-ups that are worth the trip.

versions.summary: It ranks reachable unowned cells, then compares routes to a target, back to linked territory, and via a nearby extra cell. Its board estimates account for connected income, enclosures, power-ups, rival proximity, and adjacency; it replans every eight moves or when power-ups or the route change.
versions.tagline: Plans short captures that grow connected territory and close small pockets.

versions.summary: It ranks nearby targets, then follows the best-scoring route, including routes that return to connected ground. In the watch, it expanded across the field and closed several small areas; it also picked up useful power-ups.
versions.tagline: Plans short capture-and-return routes to grow connected territory and close small areas.

versions.summary: 每回合用八步束搜索重算路线，按全盘连通收入变化评价桥接、包围以及 Deploy 和 Rollback 的实际归属效果。对高价值且靠近敌人的连接，附近形成多邻接的新连接会得到额外偏好；测试三场均获胜，实战观察也出现了修复与关键连接保护行为。
versions.tagline: 优先修复并守住家园连通收入，再紧凑扩张；进攻和热点只在收益值得时考虑。

versions.summary: It rushes a nearby hotspot, then grows from its connected border, giving one-neighbor cells useful scores. It checks nearby enclosures before rival cuts, thickens the spine every 30 ticks, and blocks rivals only within two steps of a thin point. The house-opponent watch showed multiple captures and late-game expansion.
versions.tagline: Rushes a hotspot, then expands a connected territory while making room for steady growth.

versions.summary: The frontier score now favors nearby cells more strongly, and the bot resets a repair-move counter when it is not repairing and caps each repair run at 12 moves. It keeps its existing hotspot rush, power-up choices, enclosure priorities, and spine thickening schedule.
versions.tagline: Favors nearby hotspot-rich frontier cells and limits consecutive repair turns while keeping its existing enclosure and defense plans.

versions.summary: Each move it simulates painting and small enclosures along every legal route, then chooses the first step of the highest-scoring path. It avoids Purge Cache cells and falls back to the nearest paintable cell when all path scores are nonpositive.
versions.tagline: Searches seven-step, nonrepeating routes by simulated territory income.

versions.summary: The added penalty discourages taking new cells with few supporting owned neighbors; the route search still closes real enclosures and collects useful power-ups. The watch showed 20 enclosures and power-up pickups, while testing passed all checks and finished first in all three matches; the slowest move took 20.97 ms.
versions.tagline: Searches short legal routes and favors new cells that are well supported by nearby territory.

versions.summary: Each turn, it simulates nearby paths, including enclosure flips and power-ups, then chooses the strongest first move. It avoids Purge pickups and favors compact expansion away from nearby rivals; the watches showed it growing broadly and closing small enclosures.
versions.tagline: Replans an eight-step territory search to maximize long-term income and disrupt rival territory.

versions.summary: The harmful-Purge avoidance call now runs before pickup pathfinding, so a worthwhile pickup route is planned with those cells blocked. The watched match continued expanding and taking worthwhile pickups, and all three test matches passed; incumbent and candidate returned identical scores on the test seeds.
versions.tagline: Keeps its existing compact, profitable expansion strategy while routing around rejected Purge pickups.

versions.summary: The restored planner searches six moves ahead with a width-eight beam, scoring each step by repeated gains in connected territory utility; linked cells count fully and detached cells half. It keeps the hotspot preference and pickup/Purge routing. All three house tests finished first.
versions.tagline: A six-step beam search repeatedly chooses moves that grow connected territory utility.

versions.summary: It grows through unpainted cells in the home-side wedge and strongly favors cells supported by multiple linked neighbors. When the wedge has no legal next step, it expands along the connected perimeter; it does not chase distant rivals, and it avoids Purge Cache.
versions.tagline: Builds a supported home-to-hotspot wedge, then fills its connected outer perimeter.

versions.summary: It grows from linked territory, favoring cells with multiple linked neighbors and steering early growth toward the home-side hotspot when a rival is not closer. It closes compact anchored loops, collects safe power-ups, and switches to local recovery and perimeter growth in the final 30 ticks.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected home-side wedge, closes nearby anchored loops, and collects safe power-ups.

versions.summary: The bot keeps its hotspot rush, lasso plans, power-up choices, and repairs, while normal growth plans two steps ahead and favors targets with fewer own-painted cells along the route. It limits spine widening to short own-paint routes and seeks a productive open border when boxed in.
versions.tagline: Efficient local growth with safer routes, lasso captures, and hotspot control.

versions.summary: The route search now considers paths up to eight steps, discounts later steps by 0.95, and never revisits a cell on the same route. Power-up, repair, and lasso priorities remain in place; the updated bot passed all three test matches.
versions.tagline: Chases valuable pickups, repairs supply lines, builds lassos, then searches deeper routes for the best gain.

versions.summary: Cartman favors fresh frontier cells that connect to several linked cells, while giving distant thin extensions little weight. It still closes nearby loops, takes worthwhile pickups, responds to nearby link and enclosure threats, and looks for exposed rival links when behind late in the match.
versions.tagline: Build a broad connected home, take efficient loops and pickups, and defend valuable links.

versions.summary: It searches up to 300 route nodes for safe loops, scoring painted and enclosed cells, then falls back to growing from its linked frontier. It also reconnects cut land, takes worthwhile power-ups, cuts nearby rival links, and defends weak links and hotspot rings late in the match.
versions.tagline: Grow linked territory with efficient loops, defend home ground, and steer clear of dangerous brawls.

versions.summary: The bot grows from its connected edge, favoring hotspots and moves that improve income against the projected leader. It takes worthwhile Deploy, Rollback, or Fluid pickups when the route reaches them before they disappear; the watched match also showed opponents cutting off some of its territory.
versions.tagline: Expand connected territory, swing local income, and take only pickups you can reach in time.

versions.summary: It builds a compact foundation, takes safe hotspots, seeks speed and rollback pickups, and closes small loops (larger ones when rivals are far away). It now looks for cheap supply-line cuts, favors the points leader and largest rival territory, and moves toward the open rival side when opponents cluster.
versions.tagline: Cuts valuable rival supply lines, targets the points leader and largest territory, and expands away from clustered rivals.

versions.summary: Hijacker still seeks useful power-ups, uncontested hotspots, compact enclosures, and opportunities to cut rivals off from their supply lines. It favors enemy and unclaimed cells, reconnects substantial stranded territory, and grows toward the leading rivals or an open flank.
versions.tagline: The same territory-raiding strategy, now without comments.

versions.summary: It scores fresh neighbors for value, connectivity, nearby expansion, enemy territory, and enclosure flips, then takes the best one. With no local option, it travels across linked ground to a fresh frontier and may collect a profitable pickup on a short detour; the watch showed steady expansion and useful pickups.
versions.tagline: Expand through fresh connected neighbors, using linked-ground travel only when no local paint is available.

versions.summary: It restores recent losses near home and guards vulnerable supply links, then detours for valuable pickups and closes nearby enclosures. It saves the home-side hotspot for the final 12 ticks and only targets cells that directly grow linked territory; no late hotspot push occurred in the observed matches.
versions.tagline: Protects connected ground, grabs worthwhile power-ups, and turns nearby enclosure opportunities into territory.

versions.summary: It first expands around home and along the central route, then follows randomized Hilbert infill through the middle and late game. After the opening it checks for profitable enclosures or supply-line cuts, collects power-ups only when their value exceeds travel and no opponent is closer, and avoids Purge Cache.
versions.tagline: Builds a broad connected opening, then fills Hilbert bands while diverting for profitable captures, cuts, and uncontested power-ups.

versions.summary: It first paints a compact border around home, with the zone widening as the match progresses; Hilbert filling begins at tick 90. It keeps the existing worthwhile power-up checks, avoids Purge Cache, and still takes profitable enclosure and cutoff opportunities when available.
versions.tagline: Builds a growing, connected home zone before returning to Hilbert infill and tactical attacks.

versions.summary: It keeps the compact home zone, enclosure/cut priorities, and worthwhile power-up logic. After the home phase, it grows only from the connected frontier and favors cells nearer home; power-up and tactical targets must also touch or belong to linked territory.
versions.tagline: Builds outward from home-connected territory while keeping its randomized Hilbert infill as a light guide.

versions.summary: Die Pfadsuche prüft beim Bewerten einer neuen Zelle nur, ob ein Nachbar zum verbundenen Gebiet gehört. Der Verbindungsstatus wird weiterhin entlang des Pfads weitergegeben; der übrige Spielstil bleibt unverändert.
versions.tagline: Sucht weiterhin wertvolle Pfade – und zählt eine Verbindung jetzt nur, wenn sie wirklich den verbundenen Heimatblock berührt.

versions.summary: It keeps finishing nearby enclosure loops, then expands the zone around home and pursues useful power-ups. When at least four cells are stranded, it looks for a nearby paintable bridge cell to reconnect them; in tests, the repair branch ran alongside the existing loop and defense priorities.
versions.tagline: Builds linked territory through frontier loops and quickly repairs larger cut-offs.

versions.summary: It repairs cut links and finishes active loops before choosing new frontier loops. When no loop is available, it expands with supported cells and smooth border growth; new checks skip loop-wall gaps and supported moves within three steps of an opponent.
versions.tagline: Builds a compact, loop-enclosed home zone while steering new walls and supported growth away from nearby rivals.

versions.summary: It grows from linked borders, favoring thick connections and the center, while taking nearby ×5 cells and worthwhile power-ups. It closes nearby enclosures, targets large cuts in the leader’s territory, and seeks rollback after losses reach 15 cells. Watches showed captures and major cuts; all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: Grow a connected center wedge, collect nearby bonuses, and strike valuable enemy bridges.

versions.summary: Zu Beginn versucht der Bot, den nahen Hotspot zu erreichen, bricht aber ein aussichtsloses Rennen ab. Danach wächst er verbunden, schließt lohnende Enclosures und nimmt gute Power-ups mit. Im Endspurt sichert er bei Führung Hotspots; bei Rückstand zielt er auf wertvolle gegnerische Felder und Schwachstellen.
versions.tagline: Sichert früh den nahen Hotspot, wächst verbunden weiter und kappt bei Gelegenheit gegnerische Supply Lines.

versions.summary: Fortress grows and repairs its connected home territory, favors its outer zone wall, and closes small pockets when they are nearby. Target distance and the six-step enclosure check now use its route-aware path search, which respects blocked cells and occupied routes.
versions.tagline: Builds a widening home zone, now judging targets and nearby enclosures by reachable path distance.

versions.summary: It grows a connected territory from home, reinforcing the outer edge and closing small pockets when it can. Hotspots now get an extra 1.5× value bonus, the zone radius widens at 4 + tick/6, and Instant Rollback remains blocked; the bot passed all three test matches.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected home zone that expands faster and gives hotspot cells extra priority.

versions.summary: It grows from its linked border, favoring well-supported cells, hotspots, and nearby opportunities to close small enclosures. After a cut it seeks nearby linked lost ground and rollback, avoids harmful Purge Cache pickups, and keeps its late-game growth connected.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected home zone ring by ring, then closes nearby pockets and takes safe power-ups.

versions.summary: It retakes recent nearby losses, favors new cells with several links to existing territory, and scores efficient enclosures highly. It also pursues nearby useful pickups and checks for opponent enclosure threats before expanding; against house bots it still took first place in the watched match.
versions.tagline: Hold a connected, defensible core while taking efficient enclosures, nearby pickups, and worthwhile hotspot ground.

versions.summary: It expands compactly, closes nearby pockets, and weighs hotspot premiums against travel. Repairs use simulated income changes; braces must create another path home, and Purge is avoided. Watches showed captures and useful pickups; tests passed in all three corners.
versions.tagline: Grows connected territory while comparing hotspots, repairs, pickups, and small enclosures by expected payoff.

versions.summary: It compares nearby border, hotspot and pickup routes using one simulated ownership board, including Deploy and Rollback changes to connected income. It also accounts for the route’s move timing and favors gains that arrive earlier; the watch showed broad outward growth and a Fluid pickup.
versions.tagline: Chooses routes by the connected income they actually add, while keeping Purge Cache off-limits.

versions.summary: It grows from connected cells close to home and closes small nearby enclosures when a final wall cell is available. It goes for the hotspot nearest its corner only when close, then spends the final 30 ticks targeting enemy cells whose loss would strand the most territory.
versions.tagline: Build a compact connected territory, close nearby pockets, claim the near hotspot, then sever enemy supply late.

versions.summary: It first fills a compact area near home, then retakes recent losses and reinforces its frontier. Late in the match it repairs nearby supply-line gaps and advances toward hotspots only from linked territory, while favoring routes that cross fewer of its own cells.
versions.tagline: Claims nearby ground early, defends its paint in mid-game, then pursues connected hotspots.

versions.summary: The bot grows from linked borders, favors two-neighbor growth, and lays a two-wide route before painting its nearby hotspot and outline. It prioritizes supply bridges, small enclosures, useful power-ups, and nearby late-game repairs; it targets enemy cells only when taking them strands at least three cells.
versions.tagline: Build a broad connected front, secure a reachable hotspot, and repair cuts before expanding further.

versions.summary: When at least 12 cells are stranded, it searches for a bridge of up to five paintable cells, including rival-painted cells, and repairs it when the start is close enough or 30 or more cells are stranded. In frontier scoring, every neighboring cell you do not own now counts as an exit, whether empty or rival-owned.
versions.tagline: Grows a compact home-connected zone and repairs supply cuts with the shortest available bridge.

versions.summary: It now seeks the nearest Instant Rollback when at least 15 cells lost in the last 30 ticks remain missing and one is within 12 steps; this priority comes after repairs and may cross its own paint. Its home radius grows more slowly at 7 + tick/10, encouraging the zone to fill more densely before expanding.
versions.tagline: Builds a compact home zone, repairs cutoffs, and detours for valuable power-ups.

versions.summary: It now searches up to three fresh cells ahead, scores the route using the existing frontier weights, and follows the chosen route before selecting another. Repairs and the other power-up rules remain in place; rollback detours are limited to eight steps.
versions.tagline: Chooses short, connected routes through fresh cells, while keeping its repair and power-up priorities.

versions.summary: It scores only fresh neighboring cells, favoring valuable, connected growth and nearby enclosure flips. It still repairs supply bridges and follows its existing power-up rules; the watch also showed it closing an enclosure and collecting pickups.
versions.tagline: Chooses the best immediate fresh frontier cell while keeping its repair and power-up priorities.

versions.summary: It grows outward from its linked territory and strongly prefers cells that broaden an existing patch instead of making a thin spur. In the watch, it steadily filled a large connected area; all three test matches passed without standing still.
versions.tagline: Fills broad connected patches, favoring cells supported by multiple linked neighbors.

versions.summary: It expands from its connected border and prefers cells touching multiple linked cells, keeping new territory compact. When a nearby paint would close an enclosure, it gives that move extra weight; it also favors leader-owned border cells when available.
versions.tagline: Grow connected, compact patches, close small pockets, and favor cells held by the projected leader.

versions.summary: It compares routes to hotspot cells, nearby loop closures, repairs, and enemy cuts, with eligible pickups in the same ranking. It also tries small edge-aware enclosures and falls back to connected border growth; the latest test passed all checks and won 3 of 3 built-in-bot matches.
versions.tagline: Plans short routes for hotspots, compact loops, repairs, cuts, and safe power-ups, favoring durable weighted income.

versions.summary: It opens with compact home-linked growth, favoring the least-contested reachable hotspot, then compares growth, repairs, nearby loop closures, and cuts to the strongest rival. It avoids Purge and checks pickup races before detouring; watched matches showed enclosures and rival cutoffs.
versions.tagline: Grow connected ground, close nearby loops, and choose plans by their durable score-margin value.

versions.summary: The route search paints outward from home and closes small enclosures; in the empty-opponent watch it grew across much of the field and collected Fluid Compute. It won the three built-in test matches from all three seats, with a 33.83 ms slowest move.
versions.tagline: Searches short routes for connected territory, enclosures, hotspots, and useful pickups.

versions.summary: DaisyBot compares reachable regions with all hotspots, then follows a remembered destination while favoring connected new cells. It keeps its power-up and tactical choices; the watch showed rapid growth with few steps over owned paint, and it placed first in all three tests.
versions.tagline: Expands compactly toward valuable territory while balancing payoff, travel, and competition.

versions.summary: The bot keeps its existing territory growth, repair, hotspot, and power-up choices. In both ring and bump searches, it now doubles a loop’s comparison ratio when the target hotspot is within 8 steps of linked territory and the loop flips at least one hotspot cell.
versions.tagline: Scores moves while building loops, with hotspot-enclosing loops favored near the target hotspot.

versions.summary: It keeps following its committed loops and otherwise searches for compact enclosures, then grows along its linked border when no loop is available. The loop score now doubles when the enclosed cells include a hotspot; the watch showed repeated loop closures and steady territory growth.
versions.tagline: Chains compact enclosure loops, with double priority for loops that flip hotspot cells.

versions.summary: The bot first paints the hotspot closest to its corner, then works around its outline. Once the wall is in place, it returns to growing connected territory from its border; the watch showed it reaching the hotspot and later completing an enclosure.
versions.tagline: Rush the nearest hotspot, then trace a wall around it.

versions.summary: The bot continues to prioritize vulnerable links, eligible hotspots, and short enclosure loops before its usual linked-growth scoring. Its reconnect branch now considers nearby cells with a simulated income gain above two, without checking for a minimum number of stranded cells or limiting targets to the frontier.
versions.tagline: Grows compactly from linked paint, with hotspots, short loops, and nearby reconnection gains.

versions.summary: During the first 30% of the match, the bot heads toward the nearest hotspot only when it can arrive before both rivals, painting new cells along the way. Once it owns a hotspot cell—or no hotspot qualifies—it resumes the existing decision logic; the opening rush appeared in both watch runs, and all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: Rush a reachable hotspot early, then return to compact linked growth and the existing defenses.

versions.summary: It expands near home early, reclaims recent losses, and takes worthwhile power-ups. After establishing its corner, it normally favors the weaker rival’s border, but when behind it strongly prioritizes paint belonging to the projected leader; the house-opponent watch showed both raid modes and recovery in action.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected corner, recovers stolen ground, and shifts its raids to the projected leader when behind.

versions.summary: It grows a connected area early, takes worthwhile pickups, and reclaims recently lost nearby cells. Later it raids weak ground when ahead and prioritizes leader territory when behind; the house match showed both behaviors, and it passed all three tests.
versions.tagline: Build a connected corner, recover intrusions, and hit the projected leader harder when trailing.

versions.summary: It opens toward the home-side hotspot, then steadily takes nearby cells and closes small enclosures. It only pursues worthwhile non-Purge power-ups and cuts cells from the current leader when the cut strands at least five cells; the test passed with no idle moves.
versions.tagline: Aggressively claims fresh territory, avoiding old paint unless it must cross it.

versions.summary: SlopBot favors new cells close to home that touch more of its connected territory, while still valuing hotspots and useful steals from the leader. When a nearby rival threatens a vulnerable link, it shifts priority to reinforcing that area; in the watched match it also cut off large sections of an opponent's territory.
versions.tagline: Build a compact home territory, reinforce threatened links, and cut vulnerable rival expansions.

versions.summary: It commits to one reachable hotspot early, shifts to compact connected growth mid-game, and favors predicted interception areas and vulnerable connections late. Its beam search retains enclosure and power-up scoring, with Tarjan-based risk counting each threatened cell once.
versions.tagline: A six-step planner that pursues one early hotspot, grows a sturdy home region, then contests opponents late.

versions.summary: It favors connected border cells within a home-centered radius that gradually expands. It still seeks worthwhile power-ups, targets valuable leader territory and supply-line cuts, and shifts priorities late in the match. The watch showed compact early growth followed by wider expansion, and all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: Expands a compact home zone that grows over time, while taking useful power-ups and pressuring the projected leader.

versions.summary: The bot keeps reassessing worthwhile visible items, then scores connected expansion, hotspots, enclosures, and opportunities to take territory from the leader. It now also favors new border cells beside linked cells whose loss could strand a large part of your territory; tests passed against built-in rivals.
versions.tagline: Grow connected territory while reinforcing vulnerable links, contesting valuable targets, and exploiting openings.

versions.summary: Routes targets within three steps of linked territory, with own paint costing two in path choices. In the watches it repaired links, braced threatened areas, advanced toward hotspots in loop-shaped layers, and captured enclosed cells.
versions.tagline: Builds compact, home-connected bulges, repairs breaks, and braces links under threat.

versions.summary: It measures danger from rivals near your position, then repairs links and finishes anchored loops before pursuing hotspot layers. After hotspot work, it considers all eligible power-ups together using the six-step-or-mostly-new route rule; the watch showed it closing loops and collecting pickups.
versions.tagline: A connected-growth bot that layers toward hotspots, finishes compact loops, and takes worthwhile power-ups in the restored v5 order.

versions.summary: It prioritizes completing nearby loops, repairing cut-off territory, and reclaiming stolen hotspots and nearby rival cells. It also pursues qualifying power-ups, targets vulnerable rival lines, and otherwise grows its frontier inside a radius that expands over time.
versions.tagline: Build a growing home zone by closing compact loops and defending valuable links.

versions.summary: The bot first repairs cut-off territory and reinforces nearby vulnerable cells, then pursues worthwhile power-ups and small enclosure plans. It routes with your requested ownership-weighted costs and switches to nearby gains late; tests also showed repeated repairs, pocket captures, pickups, and threat responses.
versions.tagline: Repairs weak links, captures compact pockets, and grabs valuable nearby territory.

versions.summary: Each new loop starts at its nearest unpainted wall cell, favoring the point closest to the bot. When a fresh neighboring move is available outside the base, the bot avoids routing across its own cells; its existing repair, hotspot, power-up, and cutting priorities remain.
versions.tagline: Starts each new growth loop at the frontier point nearest its current position, then works along the edge.

versions.summary: Der Bot repariert weiterhin größere Unterbrechungen und baut kompakte Schleifen. Er vergleicht die Schließzeit mit der Ankunftszeit der Gegner; wird eine laufende Schleife überholt, sucht er bevorzugt eine sichere kleinere Schleife statt zu einer einzelnen Randzelle zurückzufallen.
versions.tagline: Schließt sichere Schleifen, bevor Gegner ihre offenen Wandzellen erreichen.

versions.summary: Pogbot expands from its linked border, favoring compact growth and valuable hotspot or leader-owned cells; it also values enemy cells whose loss would strand their territory. It pursued Deploy, Rollback, and Fluid pickups in the watches, and steered away from Purge except for a severe deficit with a favorable wipe.
versions.tagline: Grows a connected home zone, grabs valuable pickups and hotspots, and pressures the projected leader.

versions.summary: It now targets the opponent with the highest accumulated score, using projected points to break ties, and favors that opponent’s paint and vulnerable links along its reachable frontier. The watch showed it closing enclosures and taking nearby useful power-ups; all three test matches passed.
versions.tagline: Grows from a connected home frontier, closes nearby loops, and pressures the opponent currently ahead on the scoreboard.

versions.summary: It takes the nearby hotspot early, then grows from connected borders while favoring valuable enclosures and cuts that strand enemy territory. It blocks imminent walls around linked land, reclaims only recent nearby losses that are worthwhile, and detours for power-ups only when their payoff clears a threshold.
versions.tagline: Claim valuable ground, close profitable enclosures, and strike enemy supply lines—especially the leader’s.

versions.summary: The bot takes its nearby hotspot early, reconnects or reclaims lost territory, and targets valuable cuts and enclosures while growing from its linked frontier. It passed all three test matches; it placed first twice and second once.
versions.tagline: Take the home-side hotspot, reclaim losses, and press the current cell leader.

versions.summary: It opens by claiming the home-side hotspot, then grows connected territory while reclaiming stolen cells and taking worthwhile power-ups. When rivals threaten its edge it shifts toward compact defense; if disconnected near the end, it compares reconnecting with a nearby cut before choosing the better payoff.
versions.tagline: Secure the nearby hotspot, keep home connected, and adapt between careful defense and efficient rival cuts.

versions.summary: It repairs cut territory first, finishes a committed pocket when only a few wall cells remain, and otherwise pursues eligible power-ups before choosing another pocket. The matches showed successful captures and retakes, with routes favoring fresh cells and linked border growth.
versions.tagline: Repairs supply lines, commits to compact pocket captures, and takes worthwhile power-ups before growing outward.

versions.summary: It repairs cut-off territory first, then thickens thin borders when an opponent is closing in and finishes a nearly complete pocket. It weighs power-ups and rival-link cuts before choosing another pocket, while keeping late moves focused on nearby valuable border cells.
versions.tagline: Repairs vulnerable links, defends against approaching rivals, and builds compact pockets for points.

versions.summary: Weighted routes guide short raids: cut a rival link, cross it, take nearby stranded paint, then return to linked territory. The bot also repairs, closes pocket plans, takes worthwhile power-ups, and targets nearby rivals late; watches showed enclosures and rival cuts, and all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: A supply-line raider that repairs its own cuts, closes small pockets, and grows aggressively.

versions.summary: It favors empty border cells that touch several of its own cells, helping fill out a connected patch instead of reaching for isolated ground. It still detours for safe, worthwhile power-ups and takes nearby enemy cells when doing so would cut off their territory.
versions.tagline: Builds valuable territory in compact patches, while still taking worthwhile pickups and easy supply-line cuts.

versions.summary: A saved loop still takes priority, while new premium loops now compete with hotspots using gain per estimated travel cost. In the watched match it pursued hotspots and completed loops; tests passed in all three matches, and the loop-over-hotspot choice occurred when its comparison favored the loop.
versions.tagline: Compares premium enclosures with hotspot gains before choosing which target to pursue.

versions.summary: Larser builds continuous loops of new cells and keeps a chosen loop unless blocked or threatened. It also reconnects valuable paint, guards threatened bridges, takes useful power-ups, and seeks hotspot steals and profitable cuts; the watches showed captures and cuts.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, capture compact pockets, and defend or attack links when the payoff is worthwhile.

versions.summary: Larser keeps expanding and closing loops, while delaying its home hotspot ring until linked ground is close enough and repairing a broken ring only when it is nearby. It now pursues useful Fluid, Deploy, or qualifying Rollback pickups within 10 cells, and scales back distant loop and expansion value late in the match.
versions.tagline: Builds connected territory, closes compact loops, secures its home hotspot, and takes worthwhile power-ups.

versions.summary: It favors broad, home-connected expansion toward the hotspot with the best real distance and rival-pressure profile. Nearby pickups, repairs, and enclosure closures must beat the estimated return from local growth; it avoids harmful Purges and discounts ground enemies can quickly retake.
versions.tagline: Build a resilient frontier toward a reachable hotspot, taking only detours that beat nearby growth.

versions.summary: Pickups, repairs, enclosures, and broad hotspot growth retain their existing logic; nearby growth comparisons now use the requested supply-delta calculation. It passed all three seat tests against varied built-in opponents, with no illegal or stationary moves and a slowest move of 15.52 ms.
versions.tagline: Grow toward a reachable hotspot while valuing new paint by its home-supply impact.

versions.summary: The test passed all three matches, and the watch showed early loops followed by linked growth, with hotspots, useful pickups, repairs, and worthwhile cuts also taking turns. Growth rewards cells with several links, and cuts are limited to nearby border cells and discounted when rivals can reconnect quickly.
versions.tagline: Grow linked territory first, while choosing loops and nearby targets by payoff per move.

versions.summary: It keeps chasing worthwhile boosts and pickups, then grows from connected borders. When behind or when rivals are fighting, it gives enemy territory and cutoffs more weight and backs off less from nearby danger; watches showed it taking enemy ground and cutting off rival cells.
versions.tagline: When behind, take bolder shots at rival territory and cutoffs instead of playing too safely.

versions.summary: The bot still prioritizes worthwhile Fluid Compute pickups, and now gives good-value Deploy pickups their own priority before other bonuses. It grows outward from connected territory, leans into attacks when behind or when rivals are fighting, and test matches showed it collecting Deploy and Fluid Compute.
versions.tagline: Build a growing home zone, chase worthwhile boosts and Deploy bursts, then attack exposed rivals.

versions.summary: It grows from linked borders and closes compact rings that flip up to 20 cells, favoring hotspots and rival territory. After step 200 it finishes an active loop, then reclaims rival border cells with hotspots first; its final moves stay connected. It avoids Purge and conditionally collects useful pickups.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, seal compact loops, and prioritize nearby hotspots and useful power-ups.

versions.summary: It takes the home-side hotspot early, then favors high-value connected growth and nearby enclosures. When behind, it looks for paint that cuts enemy income; when ahead, it reinforces exposed connections. It pursues power-ups when their payoff beats the detour and favors nearby points late.
versions.tagline: Seize the nearby hotspot, grow connected territory, and turn profitable cuts and power-ups into points.

versions.summary: It goes for the nearby hotspot, then worthwhile power-ups and profitable enemy cuts while reinforcing threatened connections. It also plans a compact enclosure near home, adding edge cells where needed; the watch showed an enclosure capture followed by connected expansion and endgame growth.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, secure the nearby hotspot, and close profitable walls and supply cuts.

versions.summary: It grows from linked territory, seeks nearby enclosures, and fills the hotspot closest to its land as the border approaches. It remembers intrusions, repairs major cuts before tightening near home, and goes for non-purge pickups nearby; late in the match it still looks for an adjacent leader neck or pickup.
versions.tagline: A compact border-grower that closes nearby pockets and takes close tactical chances.

versions.summary: It grows into new cells touching the most of its land, favors the nearest hotspot as the border reaches it, and closes pockets of 20 cells or fewer. It retakes intruder entries, repairs major cuts, targets leader cells that sever their territory, and avoids Purge Cache while collecting nearby power-ups.
versions.tagline: Expand as a compact linked border, closing nearby pockets while taking tactical openings.

versions.summary: Expansion and new loop walls stay close to linked territory, with loop choices favoring walls that touch it; when nearby rivals threaten a thin section, the bot favors widening it. It still prioritizes repairs, the nearest hotspot, power-ups, and cuts, and avoids its own paint when routing has another option.
versions.tagline: Grow from home-connected territory, repair cut-offs, and build loops that stay attached.

versions.summary: Freak goes for worthwhile nearby power-ups and claims its home zone, switching to an intruder’s corner when an opponent enters or paints its area. When a fresh paintable neighbor is available, it routes around owned cells; the watches showed it rarely stepped on its own paint while growing or retaliating.
versions.tagline: Holds a corner zone, retaliates against intruders, and favors fresh ground over owned paths.

versions.summary: The bot now uses a stronger pull toward home, increasing it in the final 50 ticks, and gives nearby enclosure-closing moves extra value. In the house match it closed several pockets and cut rival territory; it also kept its uncontested-hotspot, useful-pickup, purge-avoidance, and loop-break behavior.
versions.tagline: Build a linked home zone, close nearby pockets, and make opportunistic cuts while avoiding contested cells.

versions.summary: It claims cells near home first, then favors empty cells and rival territory that are farther from opponents. When a rival is close or it has recently lost nearby cells, it shifts toward safer border cells; the house-opponent watch showed that retreat priority activating.
versions.tagline: Fills its home territory, then expands toward open ground farther from rivals.

versions.summary: It first fills available territory near home, then expands along its connected border while favoring valuable cells and keeping distance from rivals. When it finds a nearby safe enclosure, it weighs the value of the cells it would capture and goes for the close.
versions.tagline: Grows outward cautiously, favors high-value territory, and closes safe nearby enclosures.

versions.summary: It favors linked border cells that it can reach before rivals, and halves the value of a lone linked connection. It also closes an eligible nearby hotspot wall and can take a rival choke cell that strands their territory; Purge Cache remains avoided when another move is available.
versions.tagline: Wins reachable ground first, while keeping unsupported paint for cutoffs, enclosures, or a last-resort escape.

versions.summary: Bumps score wall and captured cells by points, with extra value for hotspots and leader paint. It finishes active bumps before power-up detours, favors a nearby next bump, and keeps breach sealing first. The watched match showed repeated enclosures and rival cutoffs; the bot won all three tests.
versions.tagline: Closes safe, high-value bumps, chaining them while taking useful power-ups and pressuring the leader.

versions.summary: It grows from linked territory, closes small loops, and takes hotspots when they are within reach. It now makes out-and-back trips through fresh cells to nearby hotspot cells and power-ups, and quickly retakes recently lost neighboring cells; in the house match it also repaired cuts and answered nearby threats.
versions.tagline: Builds connected loops, reclaims nearby losses, and makes short trips for hotspots and useful power-ups.

versions.summary: The bot waits until linked territory is within four steps of an eligible hotspot, then paints a parallel lane beside the home-to-hotspot route before working on the ring. If a cut strands at least 15 cells, it can prioritize repairing the link even from far away; smaller repairs still need to be nearby.
versions.tagline: Build compact connected loops, reinforce the hotspot approach, and repair major cutoffs from anywhere.

versions.summary: A repair is now eligible from up to 12 steps away when reconnecting it restores at least 15 stranded cells; smaller reconnections remain limited to 6 steps. The rest of the loop-building, power-up, defense, and frontier strategy is unchanged.
versions.tagline: Repairs large supply-line cuts from farther away while keeping small repairs local.

versions.summary: Adds hotspot pursuit and defense, a larger compact zone, and late-game reconnection and thickening while keeping repairs, loops, cuts, and pickup rules. In the house-bot watch it reacted to hotspot threats, though it did not secure the hotspot early.
versions.tagline: Pushes toward a home-side hotspot, repairs cut links, and builds efficient compact loops.

versions.summary: It weighs own cells as costly terrain, skips most pickups with mostly-own paths, and keeps growing after a pickup rather than returning. Its loops start at the bot and follow one missing arc; the watch showed trail cuts, intruder closures, and rival classifications.
versions.tagline: Grow around the nearest hotspot, close compact loops, and route toward fresh ground instead of retracing old paint.

versions.summary: 录像中机器人持续扩张连通领地，并实际完成了小型围地；对静止对手的观察局结束时占有大片区域。三场内置对手测试均通过，且没有停步或超时报告。
versions.tagline: 从连家边界扩张，按实际路径收益权衡热点、重连与小型围地。

versions.summary: In the watched matches, it expanded from connected territory, closed several small enclosures, and sometimes cut enemy links or reconnected separated land. The updated bot passed all three built-in tests with no illegal moves, timeouts, or standing still; its slowest move was 24.27 ms.
versions.tagline: Compares practical expansion, reconnection, enclosure, power-up, and enemy-link plans before choosing a move.

versions.summary: The watched active match showed expansion, pickups, enclosures, and backup-link plans against moving opponents. Backup routes now score each cell once and persist across turns, but are rechecked for connectivity, legal steps, harmful Purges, and opponent arrival before they continue.
versions.tagline: Expands, closes pockets, and builds worthwhile alternate links.

versions.summary: It keeps the hotspot-directed border scoring and gives small enclosures first priority. It now reinforces cells threatened by nearby rivals, widens single-cell links to owned hotspots, and immediately retakes nearby lost cells; short raids return to the exact starting cell.
versions.tagline: Sweeps toward hotspots while reinforcing thin links and reclaiming nearby cuts.

versions.summary: The bot now works through hotspot areas in near-home order, taking up to ten cells in one before moving to the next. In the watches it captured all three areas, while still pursuing worthwhile power-ups and returning to broad expansion afterward.
versions.tagline: Capture ten cells in each hotspot triangle in turn, while still pursuing valuable boosts and growing connected ground.

versions.summary: It expands along its connected border first, then heads for the hotspot nearest home. In the next phase it favors nearby moves that close an enclosure, and spends the final stretch painting valuable border cells; it passed all three matches.
versions.tagline: Vrooooom out from home, whaaam the hotspot, ka-baaaaang a pocket, then finish strong.

versions.summary: It favors frontier cells with multiple neighboring cells of its own, searches more nearby U-shaped pocket shapes, and finishes pocket plans with a more generous path limit. It guards vulnerable links throughout the match, chooses a reachable hotspot to grow toward, and keeps late cut plans near its border.
versions.tagline: Builds thicker connected territory, closes nearby pockets, protects vulnerable links, and plans late rival cuts.

versions.summary: It simulates routes up to five moves ahead, favoring valuable rival paint and enclosures while discounting unsupported or distant cells. It also guards nearby critical links and makes uncontested runs for qualifying Fluid Compute or Deploy pickups; the match watch showed successful captures, cuts, and power-up pickups.
versions.tagline: Searches short, connected routes for high-value paint, enclosures, cuts, repairs, and safe power-ups.

versions.summary: Early on, Goldenbot goes for nearby hotspots reachable through connected territory and backs off from heavily contested ones. Later it pressures both rivals, takes worthwhile power-ups, and closes nearby enclosures that flip enemy territory, while favoring connected growth with open continuations.
versions.tagline: Secures connected hotspots early, then uses power-ups, enclosures, and rival pressure to grow and score.

versions.summary: It expands from its linked border unless a route to the preferred hotspot, a repair, an enclosure, a bottleneck, or a useful pickup has better projected value. It accounts for travel cells and time-weighted territory, keeps a worthwhile target while it remains valid, and returns to expansion when no special route wins.
versions.tagline: Compares special trips with connected frontier growth before committing.

versions.summary: It pursues a hotspot when its arrival looks competitive, closes nearby small enclosures, and reconnects cut-off ground when enough value is at stake. Otherwise it grows from linked borders, favors valuable rival cuts, and detours for power-ups only when their payoff justifies the trip.
versions.tagline: Builds connected territory while weighing hotspots, enclosures, repairs, cuts, and worthwhile pickups.

versions.summary: It favors connected border captures, with extra value for competitive hotspots and simulated reconnections, while also scoring nearby cuts and worthwhile pickups. In the watches it picked up power-ups, made cuts, closed short loops, and usually moved to fresh ground.
versions.tagline: Grow with fresh captures by default while comparing nearby loops, repairs, cuts, hotspots, and worthwhile pickups.

versions.summary: It searches for safe ring-shaped pockets connected to its territory, keeps painting a chosen wall in order, and favors larger pockets while Fluid Compute is active. It also closes threatened enclosures, evaluates nearby power-ups, and shifts toward rival paint and supply cuts late in the match.
versions.tagline: Builds compact safe pockets, then prioritizes tactical steals, power-ups, and late-game cuts.

versions.summary: It searches six moves ahead, valuing connected paint, small enclosures, cutoffs, and useful power-ups. Early it favors the hotspot nearest ahead of a rival; late it emphasizes reconnecting territory and stealing from the leader, falling back toward paintable ground when needed.
versions.tagline: A six-step search balances connected growth, enclosures, power-ups, and late steals.

versions.summary: VOL reconnects cut-off paint when enough territory can be restored and finishes planned loops before optional detours. It checks nearby power-ups before hotspot pursuit; the watch showed it building a wide hotspot path and growing through loops, while favoring unpainted first steps on equal-length routes.
versions.tagline: Build efficient loops, protect connected territory, and pursue reachable, uncontested hotspots.

versions.summary: Routes now consider paths up to one move longer than the shortest and favor paths that paint more unowned cells. When a rival is within six cells, new ring loops use radii 2–3; otherwise the existing radius-4 option remains.
versions.tagline: Keeps VOL’s loop-and-defense strategy, favoring fresh ground on routes and shorter loops near rivals.

versions.summary: It keeps the original outward push, fill-in phase, and rival-facing advance. When opponents threaten an enemy-painted cell at your frontier or you have a recent loss still touching linked territory, it prioritizes securing or reclaiming that ground; it also repairs supply-line gaps when nearby opportunities appear.
versions.tagline: Push outward and advance toward rivals, but secure threatened borders and repair recent losses before expanding.

versions.summary: It favors nearby border cells for connected growth instead of racing to the farthest edge. It prioritizes threatened and lost territory, avoids its own paint, and takes worthwhile power-ups beside its route; after filling behind the frontier, it shifts toward rival bases.
versions.tagline: Build a safer connected frontier from home, then turn outward toward rivals.

versions.summary: It secures the hotspot nearest home first, then grows outward from its connected border, favoring valuable cells with multiple links back to home. It detours only for nearby worthwhile power-ups and attacks enemy cells when taking them would cut off a large territory.
versions.tagline: Claims the nearest hotspot, then builds broad linked territory while taking valuable pickups and supply-line cuts.

versions.summary: It locks onto an early hotspot, finishes profitable nearby rings, and uses a six-step pruned search to favor fresh territory and worthwhile pickups. It avoids Purge Cache, penalizes recent positions, and looks for exposed enemy links. The watched match showed repeated enclosures, and all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: Claims the easiest hotspot, closes worthwhile rings, and routes each move toward connected score gains.

versions.summary: 开局朝最近的热点扩张，并在途中争取收下值得绕行的道具；有机会时会完成小型围合。其他时候优先从连通边界扩张，末段继续争取高价值地块。
versions.tagline: 先冲最近热点与高收益道具，再靠连通扩张和小型围合累积分数。

versions.summary: It keeps the existing hotspot, power-up, repair, defense, and cut priorities, then favors nearby home-side frontier cells for ordinary growth. Loop candidates are screened against the home-zone edge, and route planning charges four for each own cell versus one for new or rival paint.
versions.tagline: Closes connected loops while filling a compact, even-growing zone around home.

versions.summary: It reconnects cut-off territory with the shortest bridge, unless a qualifying Rollback is closer, and guards threatened links that could strand 10 or more cells. It keeps the existing hotspot rings and loops, counts only linked neighbors for solid growth, and widens large edge bands before continuing outward.
versions.tagline: Repairs cuts fast, guards vulnerable necks, and grows a wider linked wedge.

versions.summary: The bot now grows and extends its early edge band only from cells touching territory still linked to home. It repairs cut-off land first, then checks worthwhile power-ups before neck defense and nearby home security; hotspot goals are selected by closeness to home.
versions.tagline: A connected FAT WEDGE that repairs cuts, guards vulnerable necks, and grows only from linked land.

versions.summary: It keeps its reconnect, useful-power, enemy-distance, and timed backoff priorities before returning to enclosure building and expansion. Target routes now weigh owned cells more heavily, favoring paths that paint fresh ground; the watched match still closed enclosures and collected useful power-ups.
versions.tagline: Closes compact enclosures while favoring routes across unclaimed ground.

versions.summary: It closes an early pocket near home, then favors compact linked growth along contested borders and retakes recent losses nearby. When an opponent’s linked territory can be cut from a nearby border cell, it prioritizes that cut, and it detours for worthwhile nearby power-ups.
versions.tagline: Wall off a small corner pocket early, then defend contested ground, cut enemy links, and collect nearby power-ups.

versions.summary: Klaus first walls the corner and expands toward the center, then prioritizes reconnecting stranded territory, nearby repairs, and useful power-ups. It penalizes its own cells more strongly, gives paintable fresh cells a small baseline value, and favors fresh paths toward the frontier when deep inside its territory.
versions.tagline: Builds connected territory, repairs nearby walls, and heads back toward the frontier after deep trips.

versions.summary: It builds and scores routes of up to 20 steps, favoring loops and hotspots early while pursuing cuts and pickups when they pay off. It keeps its current plan unless another scores at least 30% better, and tries to reclaim recent lost ground when its territory is stranded.
versions.tagline: Plans short routes for enclosures, hotspots, profitable cuts, and useful power-ups.

versions.summary: It plans loops and hotspot routes while favoring cells near home and gaps beside existing territory. Against active rivals it also reconnects stranded land, widens threatened links, and looks for worthwhile cuts; repeated two-cell shuttles trigger a short escape toward fresh paint.
versions.tagline: A persistent planner that grows compactly, closes useful loops, and breaks out of repeated routes.

versions.summary: It grows connected territory and closes nearby loops, while also pursuing useful cuts and power-ups. When enough paint is stranded—or any stranded hotspot is at risk—it now accepts a bridge of up to eight unpainted cells to reconnect, and the tests show reconnection plans being used.
versions.tagline: Plans compact expansion and loops, with a more willing supply-line reconnection rule.

versions.summary: It first paints a linked route to the nearest hotspot and presses toward the center, then favors connected border cells that can keep expanding. It also looks for enclosures, cuts enemy paint when its own links are thick, reconnects only by a short route, and avoids Purge Cache.
versions.tagline: Claims the nearest hotspot, then expands in connected broad lanes, closes pockets, and takes useful pickups.

versions.summary: After a mid-game Deploy or Fluid pickup, the bot heads for the second hotspot. Once it owns that hotspot, it favors connected cells near either hotspot; the watch showed both the pickup-driven dash and the surrounding phase. Existing enclosure, supply-line, power-up, and late-growth priorities remain.
versions.tagline: Use mid-game Deploy and Fluid pickups to reach a second hotspot, then grow a connected perimeter around both hotspots.

versions.summary: It first reclaims recent losses near home, then looks for nearby leader-owned cells whose capture would strand the leader’s territory. When there’s no such cut to make, it takes power-ups whose benefit outweighs the trip, otherwise expanding along its connected border.
versions.tagline: Defend home, grow connected territory, cut the leader’s supply lines, and collect worthwhile power-ups.

versions.summary: Der Bot nimmt zuerst den erreichbaren Hotspot und lohnende Power-ups, meidet schädliche Purge-Pickups und holt verlorene Zellen in Reichweite zurück. Wenn sich eine größere Umschließung anbietet, schließt er sie; sonst erweitert er sein verbundenes Gebiet und bevorzugt wertvolle oder gegnerische Zellen.
versions.tagline: Sichert wertvolle Hotspots und Power-ups, nutzt profitable Umschließungen und wächst verbunden weiter.

versions.summary: It grows from linked border cells inside a zone that expands over the match, while nearby hotspot cells and feasible hotspot walls can take priority from that frontier. Against house bots it repaints and reconnects territory after cuts; the empty-field watch showed broad connected growth around home.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected home zone and favors nearby hotspots instead of sending out long, cuttable arms.

versions.summary: The bot no longer gives any reward to moves over its own cells; it favors new border cells in its growing home zone and still pressures active rivals. It also keeps its enclosure defense, recent-loss recovery, and worthwhile power-up detours.
versions.tagline: Keeps territory compact while choosing fresh paint over pointless walks across owned ground.

versions.summary: It first claims safe unclaimed cells near its starting corner. After that, it favors edge growth toward the opponent corner with less nearby enemy paint, while avoiding cells close to opponents; it also takes safe enclosure opportunities and cuts the leader's supply when a large cut is available.
versions.tagline: Fills its home first, then expands through connected territory along the safest, least-contested edge.

versions.summary: It reinforces vulnerable links, keeps travel closer to connected land, and favors fresh cells beside its territory. It widens the opening hotspot corridor and closes eligible nearby loops, while retaining the existing power-up and rival-link priorities.
versions.tagline: Build a compact connected territory by reinforcing weak links, favoring fresh routes, and closing efficient nearby loops.

versions.summary: The bot first repairs supply links when painting a border cell would restore income from stranded territory. Otherwise, it keeps its existing priorities: retreating from close fights, defending home, taking useful power-ups and hotspots, then growing toward valuable connected ground.
versions.tagline: Build a broad home base, pursue nearby hotspots and power-ups, and reconnect cut-off territory before expanding further.

versions.summary: It grows around home, claims nearby hotspots and worthwhile power-ups, and reconnects cut territory before expanding further. When rivals get close it favors escape and the uninvolved side; when leading or joining a wider contest, it targets reachable rival territory while keeping its usual value-focused growth.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected stronghold, then adapts its expansion and rival pressure to the match.

versions.summary: Ripidi favors new cells that stay connected, gives hotspots extra weight, and values nearby moves that close enclosures. It repairs recent losses and discounts contested ground, while detouring for beneficial power-ups and avoiding harmful ones.
versions.tagline: Grow a connected home front, close nearby pockets, and take power-ups only when their payoff is worth the trip.

versions.summary: It grows from its connected border, increasingly favoring cells near hotspots and avoiding close fights when ahead. It detours for valuable Deploys, closes nearby profitable enclosures, and repairs recent losses when they are close enough to repay the trip.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, angle toward high-value hotspots, and take worthwhile boosts without chasing every fight.

versions.summary: It heads toward the nearest unfinished hotspot, claiming only cells on its connected frontier. It builds compact triangular loops when worthwhile, scores them by value per move, rejects loops that cut linked territory, and blocks enemy walls threatening hotspots or large connected areas.
versions.tagline: Keep the hotspot rush connected, expand with compact triangles, and block walls that threaten valuable territory.

versions.summary: The bot first looks for a nearby enclosure that captures 3–9 cells, then expands from its connected border while leaning toward hotspots. When its territory is cut off, it grows from the linked frontier nearest the stranded cells to reconnect them; its existing behind-in-last-place leader attack remains in place.
versions.tagline: Grow from home, close an early pocket, and reconnect territory when opponents cut it off.

versions.summary: It heads for the inner strip beside one opponent’s border for up to 60 ticks, then expands from home, favoring empty cells over ordinary enemy paint. In the second half, it seeks nearby moves that reconnect disconnected territory and still values enemy cells that would cut their supply.
versions.tagline: Raid an enemy-side inner edge, then expand from home and repair cut supply lines late.

versions.summary: The bot expands its connected area toward cells farther from the opponents and favors cells that help fill in its existing territory. Once it has 60 linked cells, it gives nearby recently lost ground priority; a 1-in-20 roll can instead send it to a hotspot or its surrounding outline.
versions.tagline: Grow connected territory in quieter spaces, fill in your started patches, and take hotspot detours only on a 1-in-20 roll.

versions.summary: It first works toward the nearest hotspot through linked ground, then paints its perimeter. After nearby Deploy or Fluid pickups and late small enclosures, it fills paintable border cells within five steps of home before favoring outward expansion.
versions.tagline: Claims and seals the nearest hotspot, then builds a connected home zone before expanding farther.

versions.summary: It grows from the linked frontier, prioritizes repairs, small enclosures, and rival supply cuts, then looks for nearby hotspots with free cells. It only detours for close power-ups along connected paint, and in the house match it repaired cut territory and made several successful rival cuts.
versions.tagline: Builds connected, thick territory while repairing weak links and claiming nearby hotspots and worthwhile power-ups.

versions.summary: It prioritizes worthwhile pickups, genuine nearby reconnections, efficient enclosure closes, and leader bottlenecks before expanding toward the home-side hotspot. When none apply, it grows along its linked border, favors valuable or enemy-held cells, and stays closer to home late when leading.
versions.tagline: Chase profitable nearby opportunities while growing connected territory and contesting the projected leader.

versions.summary: It rushes the home-side hotspot, then favors nearby hotspots with fewer rivals and builds their enclosing walls. It ranks Fluid Compute first among worthwhile pickups, skips races an opponent can win first, and looks for nearby enemy cells whose loss would strand territory.
versions.tagline: Enclose reachable hotspots, race only for useful pickups, and break valuable enemy supply lines.

versions.summary: Weighted paths favor unclaimed, enemy, and hotspot cells over owned shortcuts while accounting for gains en route to enclosures, hotspots, and worthwhile power-ups. The house-opponent watch recorded 24 moves over owned paint and no six-step recapture cycle; all three test matches passed.
versions.tagline: Chooses objectives by durable value, then routes through territory that pays along the way.

versions.summary: It grows toward 81 tiles in its corner-side area, then pursues the nearby hotspot and enclosure opportunities. Expansion favors connected frontiers with room to grow and contested cells; when behind, it prioritizes reachable opponent territory. In the house match it expanded beyond its corner and finished ahead.
versions.tagline: Claim a corner quarter, then seize hotspots and connected ground while stealing when behind.

versions.summary: It prioritizes hotspots early, then pursues worthwhile non-purge power-ups and paint belonging to the current leader. On routes it favors new or enemy-painted cells over its own, and its border growth favors broader connected areas with a slight alternating slalom preference.
versions.tagline: Rush hotspots, collect useful power-ups, and raid the leader while widening connected territory.

versions.summary: The bot searches short additions to connected paint, confirms captures, and continues a valid route unless a materially better plan appears. It placed first in all three tested matches against built-in active opponents; worst measured move was 26.32 ms.
versions.tagline: Plans short enclosure walls and compares them with useful growth, hotspots, repairs, pickups, and supply-line cuts.

versions.summary: It reevaluates hotspot value, distance, and rival pressure each move, and only makes direct hotspot trips to nearby border cells. It tracks recent rival movement, checks vulnerable links and enclosure threats, and cools down routes that repeat. It passed all checks and placed first in all three test matches.
versions.tagline: A connected-growth strategist that recalculates hotspot value, reinforces threatened links, and breaks repeated routes.

versions.summary: It checks for small enclosures before expansion, including early on, and heads toward the chosen hotspot’s center when direct painting is out of range. Against active opponents, it prioritizes nearby reinforcement and only pursues Purge when enemy territory can be cut without risking a critical home link.
versions.tagline: Builds a connected home zone, reinforces threatened links, and pursues worthwhile enclosures and hotspots.

versions.summary: Before tick 160, routes and choices favor cells closer to your base, while still pursuing hotspots, useful power-ups, enclosures, and supply-line protection. After that preference ends, the existing priorities continue, with endgame scoring taking over near the finish.
versions.tagline: Build valuable connected territory near home early, then broaden the hunt in the final third.

versions.summary: It grows from its connected border, giving enemy-owned cells priority so each advance can steal territory and reduce an opponent's income. When there is no enemy paint on the border, it expands toward the nearer opposing home to bring the fight closer.
versions.tagline: Push connected territory toward rivals and take their paint whenever it borders your front.

versions.summary: It first paints the hotspot closest to its base. After that, it pursues worthwhile pickups and expands from its connected border, favoring cells farther from home while keeping growth attached.
versions.tagline: Claims the hotspot nearest home, collects helpful power-ups, then grows outward from connected territory.

versions.summary: The bot repeatedly paints cells along its connected border, expanding outward instead of making disconnected raids. In the empty-field watch it grew across most of the map, and it passed all three built-in tests.
versions.tagline: Grow connected territory steadily to build income throughout the match.

versions.summary: For the first half, it favors new border cells within six steps of home, keeping early growth compact. After that it paints the nearest hotspot it can claim, then favors enemy-painted cells along its border over empty cells.
versions.tagline: Build close to home early, then claim the nearest hotspot and overwrite enemy territory.

versions.summary: Zu Beginn wächst der Bot Richtung Zentrum; danach priorisiert er gestohlene Zellen nahe der Mitte, Hotspots und weiteres Zurückerobern. Die Tiefe-10-Suche beschränkt jeden Suchschritt auf die zwei aussichtsreichsten Züge und blieb in den Tests innerhalb des Zeitlimits.
versions.tagline: Expandiert, erobert Hotspots und verlorene Zellen zurück – mit Min-Max-Suche über zehn Halbzüge.

versions.summary: It takes the nearest hotspot first, then builds the largest legal ring it can find around that hotspot so the enclosed cells flip when the wall closes. It more readily detours for helpful bonuses, never steps onto a purge pickup, and otherwise favors paintable border cells belonging to the projected leader.
versions.tagline: Claims the nearest hotspot, circles a nearby area to capture it, grabs useful bonuses, and pressures the leader.

versions.summary: It favors empty front cells touching at least two linked cells, falling back to one if needed, and scores by simulated gain per step with a centerward bonus. Threat blocking now comes first, and bridge targets must be within four steps. The watch showed wedge growth and hotspot-taking; all tests passed.
versions.tagline: Builds a value-guided wide front toward the center, while handling urgent threats and profitable tactical gains first.

versions.summary: It first looks for a nearby move that closes an enclosure, then pursues its chosen hotspot and builds the surrounding wall. When those plans are complete, it pressures rival territory nearby—aiming at the points leader in second place and the second-place bot when last—and otherwise expands along its connected border.
versions.tagline: Close nearby enclosures first, secure an uncontested hotspot, then steal from the rival specified by your standing.

versions.summary: It keeps its hotspot-and-wall plan, closes nearby enclosures, and takes useful power-ups reachable before the next wave. It favors cells farther from opponents, defends vulnerable links, and targets ranked rivals or enemy supply lines nearby. Multi-step route scoring favors safer choices.
versions.tagline: Secure quiet ground, protect supply lines, and choose safer multi-step routes.

versions.summary: Races to every power-up wherever it is, Purge Cache included, and waits for the next ones in the middle of the field, where its paint gets cut off.
versions.tagline: Races for every power-up wherever it is, Purge Cache included, and waits for the next ones in the middle.

versions.summary: It grows outward from the home corner, favoring new cells supported by at least two of its own. When paint is cut off, it seeks a short reconnection; it also targets nearby leader cells whose capture would strand territory, closes nearby small enclosures, and takes useful nearby power-ups while avoiding Purge.
versions.tagline: Builds a dense home territory, reconnects severed paint, and cuts nearby leader supply lines.

versions.summary: Der Bot füllt zuerst nahe freie Randzellen, nimmt nur sichere Hotspot-Zellen direkt an seiner Front und schließt kleine sichere Löcher. Er meidet Zellen innerhalb von drei Schritten zu Gegnern und holt nahe, lohnende Power-ups; Purge Cache lässt er aus.
versions.tagline: Wächst in verbundenen, sicheren Wellen von der Heimatecke nach außen.

versions.summary: It first heads for paintable cells taken from you recently or earlier, when they are within reach. Otherwise it walks triangular paths from home that grow from size 3 to 14, then favors nearby border cells beside the closest opponent.
versions.tagline: Reclaim stolen ground first, then trace expanding triangles while shadowing the nearest rival.

versions.summary: It first retakes recently lost cells, then paints progressively larger triangular paths from home. Once those paths are painted, it grows from its connected border, favoring fresh cells near the triangle and the closest rival.
versions.tagline: Reclaim stolen ground, trace expanding triangles, and shadow the nearest rival while favoring fresh cells near the shape.

versions.summary: It repeatedly builds small enclosure loops from linked territory, and the watches confirmed that these loops close and flip nearby cells. When its repair threshold is met it reconnects stranded land; it also detours for valuable non-purge power-ups, then grows toward high-value frontier cells when no loop is active.
versions.tagline: Repairs broken links, takes worthwhile power-ups, and closes compact loops before growing its frontier.

versions.summary: Der Bot bevorzugt neue Zellen, die an sein verbundenes Gebiet grenzen, und wächst so stetig nach außen. Im Test blieb er in Bewegung und nahm regelmäßig weiteres Gebiet ein.
versions.tagline: Wächst Schritt für Schritt über die eigene Grenze hinaus.

versions.summary: Juliean wächst überwiegend entlang der eigenen Front und gibt Schritten über bereits eigene Felder einen Malus von −0,3. Es verstärkt bedrohte Verbindungen, wenn Gegner nahe sind, nimmt lohnende Power-ups mit und nutzt erreichbare Schnitte gegen gegnerische Verbindungen.
versions.tagline: Bleibt an der Front, färbt bevorzugt neues Gebiet und nimmt nur lohnende Umwege.

versions.summary: The bot heads straight for the hotspot nearest its corner, then paints the surrounding outline in order. Once the wall is built, it grows from its linked border while keeping the wall repaired if opponents take a section.
versions.tagline: Rush the nearest hotspot, then build and maintain a wall around it.

versions.summary: It rushes hotspots, paints their outlines, then favors farther new territory. It avoids routes over its own cells and keeps moving when a path is blocked, using own ground only when needed to get unstuck.
versions.tagline: Chases hotspots and expands outward, avoiding its own painted ground whenever it can.

versions.summary: Fills a zone around its home corner that grows until mid-field, then barely leaves it. Compact and hard to cut off, but it leaves most of the field to others.
versions.tagline: Defends a zone around its corner that grows until mid-field, then barely leaves it.

versions.summary: The bot heads for the hotspot nearest home, then widens the route with cells that stay connected. It closes small legal loops, takes useful nearby power-ups, and thickens or repairs ground when a rival approaches; late growth favors rival territory, with safe connected painting in the final 15 turns.
versions.tagline: Claim a nearby hotspot, keep growth connected, and reinforce the route when rivals press close.

versions.summary: The bot first takes the hotspot nearest home, then switches between rivals and favors the one with the largest connected territory, including nearby open cells. When recent stolen cells point to an opponent attacking nearby, it redirects its attack to the other rival; a successful steal starts a new round of pressure.
versions.tagline: Claim a hotspot, then keep both rivals in the fight by attacking connected territory.

versions.summary: It rushes the hotspot nearest home and paints its outline when the enclosure can flip cells. It avoids Purge Cache, takes worthwhile power-ups only when close, and otherwise grows near its base while favoring nearby leader territory that would cut supply lines.
versions.tagline: Claims the nearest hotspot, walls it in, and looks for nearby chances to disrupt the leader.

versions.summary: It targets hotspots only when it can arrive at least two steps ahead, then paints their outline; when rivals contest one, it turns to the alternate. It favors valuable kettles and thick fresh borders, takes nearby Deploy and Fluid Compute, and makes large cuts into the leader’s territory only when behind.
versions.tagline: Wins reachable hotspot races, builds compact high-value kettles, and keeps expansion connected while avoiding rival bases.

versions.summary: It favors compact border growth and valuable hotspot cells, and takes nearby enemy cells when doing so can cut off their territory. When its own paint is stranded, it seeks nearby bridges to reconnect it; it also takes worthwhile Deploy pickups and adjusts aggression based on the current lead.
versions.tagline: Grow connected territory, exploit valuable supply cuts, and shift between safe expansion and attacks on the leader.

versions.summary: It expands from the home-linked frontier and weighs captures along a route against its travel time and nearby threats. It also competed for hotspots, pickups, repairs, closures, and cuts; it avoided harmful Purge Cache and held its lead in the tested matches.
versions.tagline: Grow connected territory while comparing short routes by lasting value, travel, and exposure.

versions.summary: It grows from the home-linked frontier and charges owned-cell travel for the expansion it gives up. Hotspots, closures, repairs, cuts, and useful pickups compete in the same route comparison; watches showed these tactics in play, and all three tests passed.
versions.tagline: Builds connected territory while comparing detours against productive home-frontier growth.

versions.summary: Most turns, Scorekeeper grows along its home-linked border. It also takes hotspots and pickups when their payoff justifies the trip, and sometimes closes pockets or restores lost connections; the watched match showed each of those actions except link guarding and enclosure blocking.
versions.tagline: Durable growth, with defenses and special targets judged against the value of expanding.

versions.summary: It builds a home-to-hotspot spine, claims the hotspot, and works through feasible loops along the spine and near home. It prioritizes reconnecting the largest stranded patch, useful nearby power-ups, vulnerable rival links, and widening threatened spine sections; late in the match it stays close to its territory.
versions.tagline: Connects the nearest hotspot, closes compact loops, and reacts to rivals and useful power-ups.

versions.summary: Blobby closes a wall around home, takes each of the two closest hotspots fully, and adds a surrounding enclosure when possible. It pursues valuable Fluid or Rollback pickups, looks for a nearby closure after an enemy capture, and grows outward from its border otherwise.
versions.tagline: Build a compact home enclosure, secure both nearby hotspots, and chase worthwhile Fluid and Rollback boosts.

versions.summary: It compares non-repeating routes by linked territory value, hotspot cells, small enclosures, and cut-point risk near rivals. In the watched match it expanded across the field, closed pockets, and collected power-ups; when no route scored positively, it headed for a linked border cell.
versions.tagline: Search five-step routes for valuable connected territory while pricing in cut risk.

versions.summary: It expands from linked territory until a rival comes into contact, then favors valuable border trades backed by several linked neighbors and closer to home. When both rivals pressure it, it disrupts one—choosing the closer rival, with territory size breaking ties—and takes only worthwhile nearby pickups.
versions.tagline: Grow from home, then trade and disrupt while keeping your territory compact.

versions.summary: It first moves toward its chosen nearby hotspot, then expands from connected borders and closes small enclosures when they offer enough value. It interrupts growth for valuable nearby repairs or pickups, avoids Purge Cache, and clears a loop plan when it is completed or blocked.
versions.tagline: Secure a nearby hotspot, then grow compactly with connected loops, timely repairs, and worthwhile pickups.

versions.summary: It grows from linked border cells, favoring high-value ground, and pursues worthwhile power-ups while steering clear of harmful purges. It also takes the home-side hotspot and closes nearby enclosures when possible; tests passed against the built-in bots.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, seize valuable hotspots, and take power-ups or enclosures when the payoff is worthwhile.

versions.summary: The bot now evaluates routes with a 240-evaluation budget while keeping the 16-path beam and replanning each move. It captured several enclosed pockets and picked up Fluid Compute and Deploy in the watched matches; against active rivals it also responded to cut territory through its existing route scoring.
versions.tagline: A wider route search weighs defensible territory, captures, and pickups before choosing its next step.

versions.summary: The bot first paints a planned ring near home, then favors leader-owned border cells and nearby enclosure-closing moves. In the final phase it paints the outlines of the hotspot triangles, pursues a non-purge power-up once per phase, and avoids purge caches.
versions.tagline: Surround home early, strike the leader’s weak links, then encircle the hotspots.

versions.summary: It first pursues the nearest hotspot, reconnects stranded territory, and takes enemy border cells that would sever their supply. When standing on its own paint, it prioritizes claiming available border cells instead of detouring toward a particular enemy home; this new phase appeared frequently in the match checks.
versions.tagline: Claims its nearest hotspot, repairs cut links, and quickly expands from its own territory.

versions.summary: It grows from linked borders, favoring hotspots and rival territory, while reclaiming recent losses and closing nearby pockets. It skips harmful Purge Cache pickups and detours for worthwhile power-ups; against house bots it recovered stolen ground, made several captures, and won.
versions.tagline: Build connected territory, cash in nearby power-ups, and turn small enclosures into extra ground.

versions.summary: The bot keeps expanding from its linked border and favors cells with greater point value, including hotspots and enemy territory it can take. In the empty-field watch it steadily spread across the board and completed several small enclosures.
versions.tagline: Claim as much valuable connected territory as possible, one border cell at a time.

versions.summary: It keeps working on the nearby hotspot first, then detours for power-ups whose payoff beats the travel cost. From there it targets nearby enemy cells that would strand their territory, otherwise expanding along its connected border; harmful Purge Cache pickups are avoided.
versions.tagline: Claims its nearby +5 hotspot, grabs worthwhile power-ups, and cuts enemy supply lines from connected ground.

versions.summary: The bot repeatedly grows from its linked border, favoring cells closer to the map center and giving hotspot cells a strong bonus. It claimed hotspot ground during the watched match while continuing its centerward expansion.
versions.tagline: Push outward from connected territory toward the middle, claiming hotspot cells when they lie along the way.
